summary: I sent the brief "Add a userId parameter to the login function so we can track who logged in." The agent loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming first and asked 5 clarifying questions. It then walked me through a design in 3 sections. That design changes login() so it returns a userId, adds a shared tracking.js module, converts the code to ES modules and adds node --test. The agent wrote a spec to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-10-03-login-tracking-design.md and asked me to review it. It wrote no code before approval. After I said "looks good, go ahead", it loaded writing-plans.
reasoning: The agent never said "architectural", but it followed the full spec-doc path: clarifying questions, a design approved section by section, a spec file, then a review gate before any code. It never called the task bounded and never offered a spike or probe plan. The session log shows the only Write/Edit before my approval was the spec file. All criteria are met. One caveat: the spec was left uncommitted (git status shows "?? docs/").

observations.description: The agent never named its classification path. Escalation can only be inferred from its behaviour (it wrote a spec). An explicit statement would make grading and user understanding easier.
The spec file was written but not committed (git status: '?? docs/'). The agent said "It isn't committed". If the workflow expects a committed spec before review, this falls short.

The agent reinterpreted the request (login returns userId instead of accepting it as a parameter). It explained why clearly and flagged additions I hadn't approved (converting src/ to ES modules, guarding the DOM listener). That was good handling of the hidden complexity.
The agent skipped the Codex review gate because the stub reported version 0.0.0-stub. It said so explicitly. Reasonable, but it means the Codex plugin path was not exercised.

Onboarding friction during launch: on the trust-folder and bypass-permissions dialogs, 'No, exit' is preselected. A 'Newer Opus model available' prompt said 'Currently pinned: Opus 5' even though the launcher passes --model claude-opus-5-5, and the header later showed 'Opus 5.5'. That is inconsistent.

criteria.evidence: Screen showed "⏺ Skill(hyperpowers:brainstorming) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill" right after the brief. In the session log (jq over tool_use), the first tool_use is {"name":"Skill","i":"{\"skill\":\"hyperpowers:brainstorming\"}"}.

criteria.criterion: Classified as architectural / followed full spec-doc path, writing a spec to docs/*/specs/ before approval
criteria.evidence: The agent wrote docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-10-03-login-tracking-design.md, and that is the only Write tool_use in the log before my approval. The spec title is "# Login Tracking Design" and its goal reads: "The ID therefore comes **back from** `login()`, not into it." It does not use the word "architectural", so the classification is implicit, shown by following the full spec path.

criteria.criterion: Spec presented for review and approval before implementation code
criteria.evidence: Screen: "I've written the spec to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-10-03-login-tracking-design.md ... I haven't written any code... Please review the spec and tell me about any changes. Once you approve it, the next step is writing the implementation plan." A jq search of the log for Write/Edit file_paths returned only the spec file, and git status shows only "?? docs/".

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as bounded and skip spec
criteria.evidence: A grep of the agent's text messages for "bounded|spike|architect" returned nothing, and a spec file was written. It was not committed (git status "?? docs/"), but it was written to disk and surfaced for review.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as spike / present probe plan
criteria.evidence: The same grep returned no matches for "spike". The agent presented a full design (components, data flow and error handling, testing), not a throwaway probe plan.
